title: Dispatch latency: developer starts minutes late or never
description: dispatch.sh marks the issue in_progress before typing the prompt into the developer pane, but 'bd ready' (what the developer's idle loop polls) excludes in_progress issues. If the pane is inside its bounded blocking poll (15 x 30s), the typed prompt only queues until the Bash call returns — up to 7.5 min — and the poll itself can no longer see the dispatched issue, so it waits out the full window. If the keystroke is lost entirely, the issue never reappears in 'bd ready' and the developer idles forever. Fix: leave the issue open on dispatch (developer claims it), and interrupt a pane that is provably idle-waiting so a dispatch/message is read within seconds.
close_reason: dispatch leaves issues open (bd ready backstop) + idle wake; shared 30s idle_wait.sh for all three agents

title: Agent panes: modal popup storm blocks input
description: notify_header.sh uses a modal 'tmux display-popup -E ... sleep 4' which grabs the keyboard. Combined with debugger.sh/tester.sh piping interactive claude through 'tee' (claude sees a non-TTY stdout, exits immediately, restart loop fires every 15s), this produces a popup on top of the workspace every few seconds and makes the session unusable.

title: Named sessions (-s) don't reach the agent panes: SESSION_NAME falls back to 'multiagents'
description:
Agent panes are started with 'tmux send-keys', so their shell inherits the TMUX SERVER's environment, not workspace.sh's. SESSION_NAME is unset there, and config/workspace.conf then defaults it: export SESSION_NAME=${SESSION_NAME:-multiagents}. Only watcher.sh gets the real name, because it is launched as a genuine child with the variable passed explicitly.

Consequences when started as 'workspace -s myproj':
- watcher.sh writes /tmp/multiagents-myproj/watcher.log, while runner.sh creates its FIFO and streams output under /tmp/multiagents-multiagents/ — the session's output is split across two state dirs.
- Agents calling notify.sh/msg.sh/dispatch.sh with $SESSION_NAME target the session named 'multiagents', which may not exist or may be a DIFFERENT running workspace.
- Two concurrently running named workspaces collide on the same /tmp/multiagents-multiagents/ state dir (idle heartbeats, tester-head, runner FIFO).

Not hit with the default session name, since the fallback happens to match — which is why this has gone unnoticed.

Repro: workspace -s e2e4 ; the runner pane prints '[runner] and stream to /tmp/multiagents-multiagents/watcher.log' instead of .../multiagents-e2e4/...

Fix: prefix each agent launch in workspace.sh with the real value, e.g. tmux send-keys -t "$BR" "SESSION_NAME=$SESSION_NAME $SCRIPT_DIR/scripts/agents/tester.sh" Enter (4 call sites: orchestrator, developer, tester, runner).

title: Remove the [ Logs ] button pane and its popup viewer
description: The bottom 2-line logs button pane and its click-to-open watcher-log popup are unused in practice. Delete the pane, scripts/logs_button.sh, scripts/show_watcher_log.sh and the MouseDown1Pane popup binding, and simplify resize_panes.sh to the two remaining columns. The hidden runner window, run_in_watcher.sh and watcher.sh all stay: watcher.log is still written and still streams live, it is just read with tail -f instead of by clicking.

title: Remove debugger pane: 3-pane layout (orchestrator left, developer+tester right)
description: Delete the debugger agent entirely and reshape the tmux workspace from a 2x2 grid into a 3-pane layout: orchestrator full-height on the left, developer top-right, tester bottom-right, logs button full-width at the bottom. The tester absorbs the debugger's fix-failing-tests loop: it writes tests, runs them, fixes production code when they fail, then files the validation issue for the orchestrator. Touches workspace.sh, config/workspace.conf, scripts/resize_panes.sh, scripts/idle_wait.sh, scripts/msg.sh, scripts/agents/*, agents/*.md, README.org, beads-workflow.org.
close_reason: 3-pane layout shipped: orchestrator full-height left, developer top-right, tester bottom-right. Debugger agent removed; tester absorbed the fix-failing-tests loop.

title: Tester and debugger poll on model turns, not a 30s loop
description: tester.sh and debugger.sh hand the idle model a prose instruction ('run <cmd> every 30 seconds') instead of one literal blocking loop like developer.sh does. Each iteration is then a whole model turn, so the real interval is unbounded and typically well over 30s. Fix: share one bounded 30s/iteration wait loop (scripts/idle_wait.sh) across developer, tester and debugger.
close_reason: dispatch leaves issues open (bd ready backstop) + idle wake; shared 30s idle_wait.sh for all three agents

title: Drop sync.sh: leave branch management to the user
description: scripts/sync.sh rebases between features/<name> and test/<name>, and the agent instructions/docs assume those branches exist. Remove the script and the branch-per-role workflow so agents operate on whatever branch the user has checked out.

title: Add peer-to-peer agent messaging (scripts/msg.sh)
description: Agents can currently only talk along fixed edges: dispatch.sh (->developer), notify.sh (->orchestrator), and debugger.md hand-rolls raw tmux send-keys to reach the tester. Ad-hoc questions between any two roles have no supported path. Add scripts/msg.sh <to-role> <message> that resolves any pane by @role, stamps the sender role from the calling pane, and document it in all four agent files + README.
close_reason: Implemented scripts/msg.sh; documented in all four agent files and README
